concerns.text: T028b mandates PGLS for N >= 10, but Constitution Principle VI explicitly mandates 'Spearman rank correlation' for all correlation analyses. The task silently relaxes the constitutional constraint by substituting PGLS for Spearman without a spec amendment authorizing this methodological shift.

T029 mandates 'Permutation-based FDR' as primary and relegates Benjamini-Hochberg (BH) to secondary. Constitution Principle VI explicitly mandates 'Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction' as the method for statistical significance. This task violates the constitutional constraint by demoting the mandated method.

T029 introduces 'Phylogenetic Independent Contrasts (PIC) shuffling' to generate the null distribution. Neither the Spec (FR-005) nor the Constitution authorizes PIC shuffling for FDR correction. This introduces an unapproved statistical technique, violating the constraint that methods must be strictly defined in the spec/constitution.

T057 pre-filters features present in < 10% of isolates. FR-002 requires the system to extract and report *all* virulence-associated gene profiles. Filtering rare features before analysis violates the requirement to report all extracted features, effectively weakening the data completeness constraint.

T031b generates a 'Descriptive Case Study' for N < 10. While the Plan mentions this fallback, the Spec (FR-004) mandates PGLS computation without defining a statistical fallback for small N. The task implements a workaround that bypasses the FR mandate without an explicit spec amendment allowing the skip of statistical analysis.
